Comparison with similar homes
The property is assessed at $31.18 per square foot of building area. The median of 20 similar homes in the
same Assessor neighborhood is $30.59 per square foot, so the property is 2% above the median.
13 of the 20 comparable homes are assessed lower per square foot than the property. The property ranks at
the 65th percentile of the comparable homes by AV per square foot.
How comparable homes were chosen: same neighborhood, class 205, building sqft within ±25%, built within
±15 years (Assessor neighborhood 27080), excluding multi-building parcels and homes without recorded
square footage. The 20 most similar by size, age, baths, land and construction are listed on page 2.
Uniformity figure
Applying the comparable homes' median of $30.59 per square foot to the property's 1,668 square feet gives
an assessed value of $51,028. That is $972 less than the current assessed value of $52,000.

Filing steps: Cook County Board of Review
PIN 16-17-121-030-0000 · Tax year 2026
Page 3 of 3
AssessGap is not affiliated with Cook County. You file and sign your own appeal.
How a homeowner files their own appeal, from the Board of Review's published instructions and rules (checked
2026-11-24). Rules and dates change; the Board's website is the final word. This is general information, not legal
advice. You file, sign and present your own appeal.
1.
Oak Park Township's 2026 Board of Review window closed on September 1, 2026. Check
https://www.cookcountyboardofreview.com/dates-and-deadlines for next year's dates.
2.
Take a color photo of the front of your home. The Board's Rule 14 requires one, taken within the last
12 months, in the brief you upload. Mark the date it was taken. Photos of the comparable homes are
encouraged.
3.
Check the details on page 2 (square feet, year built, bedrooms, baths) against your home. If the
Assessor has something wrong, say so in your brief.
4.
Go to https://appeals.cookcountyboardofreview.com/ and choose Submit an Appeal. You can create
an account or continue as a guest (guests get the decision by mail only; account holders also get it
by email).
5.
Choose "Property Over-Assessed" as the type of appeal and enter PIN 16-17-121-030-0000. When
asked if you are a Board of Review attorney, answer No. Choose your appellant type (owner).
6.
Decide whether you want a hearing. It is optional, held by phone for homeowners, and the Board
says you are not penalized for skipping it. You choose this when you file.
7.
Enter comparable properties if you like (optional: the Board's analysts also pull their own). The PINs
on page 2 are similar homes assessed lower per square foot than yours, from the same
neighborhood and class.
8.
Review, initial, confirm and submit before the deadline. Save your complaint number.
9.
Upload your evidence after submitting: your brief with the photo, and this report if you wish, by the
evidence deadline for your township.
10.
Watch for the decision, usually 8–16 weeks after your township closes. You can check status at
https://apps.cookcountyil.gov/BORDecisionSearch/. A re-review must be requested within 3 days of
the decision letter. If you disagree with the decision, you can appeal to the state Property Tax
Appeal Board within 30 days, and you can appeal again next year.
AssessGap is not affiliated with Cook County. You file and sign your own appeal. This compares Cook County assessed
values (AV) and AV per building square foot among similar homes, using public Assessor data. It is not an appraisal and
does not estimate what any property would sell for.
